topic: Adoption-aligned uniform event-curve inference for staggered MNAR low-rank panels. Fix the eligible-cohort unit-share event estimand and use the exact Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 block influence coefficients. Derive a uniform growing-dimensional influence representation, the full staircase-overlap covariance including shared donor-cell terms, a consistent heteroskedastic plug-in covariance, and honest studentized Gaussian-multiplier bands. Determine the weakest primitive uniform remainder envelope built from the published Choi--Yuan block ratios and prove a legal counterarray for every strictly weaker envelope claimed sharp. Use the rank-one two-horizon witness whose shared pre-treatment cell has coefficient 1/4 in each expansion and covariance product 1/16; apply the result to the Ben-Michael--Feller RTC-law event curve. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Cohort aggregation of Proposition A.4 yields the standardized array D_n^-1(tau_hat-tau)=-sum_q a_.q e_q+rho_n with unit marginal variances and maximum coefficient L_n(K). Standard high-dimensional approximation applies under the stated leverage condition. The presolve derived a sufficient primitive envelope Delta_CY,n(K)sqrt(log(K vee 2))->0 by combining the joint remainder bound with Gaussian anti-concentration. In the balanced rank-one instance, each horizon has variance 3/4; four shared pre-treatment cells contribute covariance 1/4, hence correlation 1/3. Focused checks found only scalar or fixed-functional inference, not growing event-curve coverage. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct Choi--Yuan-legal triangular arrays whose standardized nonlinear remainder attains the Delta_CY scale strongly enough to prove that every strictly weaker simultaneous-band envelope fails. EARLY KILL TEST: Compute the exact second-order remainder in a balanced strong-factor rank-one panel with equally split cohorts and growing K; pivot the sharp-envelope claim if it is uniformly little-o of Delta_CY for every legal split, because the required converse family would then lack an attainable witness.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the eligible-cohort unit-share event-time ATT built from Choi--Yuan's exact Proposition A.4 block estimators admit honest studentized simultaneous bands over a growing horizon set, with covariance retaining every shared treated- and donor-cell term?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives debiased asymptotically normal inference for MNAR matrix completion and a heteroskedastic block-missing extension, but its published inferential targets are scalar or blockwise rather than a growing event curve.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The discussion says event-time aggregation crosses calendar times and right factors, so both asymptotic normality and variance differ from Choi--Yuan's calendar-time target, and it calls for staggered heteroskedastic variance estimation.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael and Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association, discussion paper

source_refs.claim: For staggered DiD group-time effects, the paper proves validity of a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous rather than merely pointwise inference, showing that whole-path coverage is a separate theorem.
source_refs.author: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

source_refs.excerpt: Its contribution is the DDD-specific shared-cell covariance mapping
add a primitive condition proving inf_t sigma_Jn(t)>0 and uniform consistency of sigmahat_Jn

open_problems.why_unsolved: Choi--Yuan's scalar block expansion does not itself yield the joint law after adoption-aligned aggregation: a primitive pre-treatment or donor-cell error can enter several event horizons, so cohortwise independence deletes off-diagonal coefficient products, including the proposed two-horizon witness's 1/16 term. Ben-Michael--Feller identify this event-time boundary, while the banked DDD result handles shared cells only in a fixed finite score stack and its reviewers reject high-level covariance consistency in favor of primitive uniform rates. The missing work is to aggregate the exact Proposition A.4 coefficients first, derive the full staircase covariance, control the nonlinear remainder uniformly in K, and prove heteroskedastic plug-in and multiplier validity under the published block ratios and leverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving a uniform K-dimensional representation D_n^{-1}(hat_tau-tau) = -sum_q a_{·q}e_q + r_n, the full covariance Sigma_{kk'} = sum_q a_{kq}a_{k'q}sigma_q^2, a uniformly consistent heteroskedastic plug-in Sigma_hat, and conditional Gaussian-multiplier sup-t bands with asymptotic simultaneous coverage as K grows.

writing_exemplar.why: Its calendar-time-versus-event-time last-mile framing lands directly on the target estimand and the RTC-law application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Choi--Yuan make structured MNAR completion inferentially usable -> applied staggered-policy work wants effects indexed by exposure duration -> event-time aggregation crosses calendar factors and changes covariance -> derive honest whole-curve uncertainty for the RTC-law event path

method_exemplars.technique: Use the exact block debiasing expansion and its heteroskedastic residual-variance proof, aggregate the published cell coefficients, and only then form cross-horizon covariance products.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired event curve is a linear aggregation of precisely these MNAR block estimates, so Proposition A.4 supplies the load-bearing influence coefficients.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Gaussian approximation and the conditional Gaussian multiplier bootstrap to maxima of sums of independent high-dimensional vectors with unrestricted coordinate correlation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once each primitive panel error is represented by its K-vector of event-horizon coefficients, the studentized event-curve supremum is a maximum of one correlated high-dimensional vector sum.

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate cohort-time influence functions to event time and bootstrap one sup-t critical value for simultaneous path coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest econometric whole-event-curve inference template; the exact Choi--Yuan coefficients replace its DiD influence functions.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the attainable necessary-and-sufficient primitive uniform remainder envelope for growing-dimensional Choi--Yuan event-curve bands, and can every strictly weaker claimed envelope be defeated by a Choi--Yuan-legal low-rank staggered-adoption triangular array?

source_refs.claim: The paper's blockwise asymptotic normality uses explicit low-rank perturbation and debiasing remainders under block-ratio, incoherence, and signal conditions, but it does not identify an attainable sharp simultaneous remainder frontier.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that converting a uniform linearization into honest bands requires an anti-concentration-scale remainder condition and develops Gaussian-multiplier bands without a fixed supremum limit law.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: The paper proves dimension- and envelope-sharp Gaussian and bootstrap approximation bounds for bounded high-dimensional vector sums, but its lower-bound arrays are not constrained to arise from low-rank MNAR panel completion.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Yuta Koike

source_refs.excerpt: the necessity frontier for an uninflated multiplier band remains open
Resolve the band-necessity OEQ with an explicit nondegenerate undercoverage packing tied to a named nuisance

open_problems.why_unsolved: Gaussian anti-concentration gives sufficiency once a joint Choi--Yuan remainder bound is available, and the prior functional-DiD run explicitly leaves necessity of an uninflated-band condition open. Sharpness, however, needs an attained nonlinear remainder with the correct sign and scale. Generic high-dimensional lower-bound arrays need not come from one incoherent low-rank mean matrix, a nested adoption staircase, legal block ratios, and the Proposition A.4 debiasing map. The first changed proof step is therefore the lower-bound construction: compute the exact second-order remainder in a balanced strong-factor rank-one panel and embed it across growing horizons; if every legal split makes it uniformly little-o of Delta_CY,n, the advertised Delta_CY frontier must be replaced by the smaller attainable scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp-frontier theorem identifying an explicit attainable Delta_star,n(K) whose product with sqrt(log(K vee 2)) tending to zero suffices for honest bands and, for every strictly weaker envelope, a legal staggered-MNAR triangular array with nonvanishing simultaneous coverage error, or a counterexample theorem proving Delta_CY unattainable and deriving the smaller frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its weak-signal MNAR framing and explicit primitive block ratios provide the natural language in which a sharp remainder frontier should be stated.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: MNAR block splitting permits weak-signal scalar inference -> event-curve inference needs those expansions uniformly over many horizons -> anti-concentration magnifies nonlinear error at the maximum -> determine the exact attainable primitive threshold rather than only a sufficient rate

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian supremum anti-concentration to translate an attained uniform coupling remainder into a quantitative coverage-error bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It isolates the proof location where a sqrt(log K)-scale remainder becomes load-bearing for honest band validity.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its matching upper/lower approximation strategy and envelope-sensitive lower-bound arrays while enforcing the Choi--Yuan factor and adoption constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired conclusion is likewise a sharp envelope boundary, but for a narrower model-generated vector class.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand the debiased block estimator to exact second order and track block ratios, singular-space perturbations, and coefficient leverage without replacing them by coarse maxima.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Only this proof reveals whether the nominal Delta_CY bound is attainable by a legal panel or is an artifact of successive inequalities.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct honest bias-aware simultaneous event-curve bands for staggered MNAR panels whose untreated mean matrix is only approximately low rank, with coverage uniform over an explicit singular-value-tail class relevant to the ill-conditioned RTC panel?

source_refs.claim: The RTC discussion reports condition numbers around 100--10,000 and a long tail of small but non-negligible latent factors in a state-policy panel with only about 50 units and periods.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael and Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association, discussion paper

source_refs.claim: The paper proves entrywise and scalar treatment-effect inference for approximate-factor low-rank completion without sample splitting, but not bias-aware simultaneous inference for a growing staggered event path.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that rank over-specification can generate non-negligible ridge-type bias, so factor-tail uncertainty is not automatically absorbed into variance.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Weak leading factors and an approximate low-rank tail are different obstacles: the tail induces horizon-dependent deterministic projection bias that can align across the supremum and is absent from the cell-noise covariance. The RTC application makes the boundary substantive because severe conditioning, a long factor tail, and few states coexist. The first step beyond scalar approximate-factor inference is to push a primitive weighted nuclear- or operator-norm tail budget through the adoption-aligned Proposition A.4 coefficient array and solve for the worst-case studentized joint bias across all horizons.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sensitivity-band theorem giving the sharp joint bias radius induced by a stated singular-value-tail class, adding it to a multiplier stochastic band, and proving uniform simultaneous coverage plus a breakdown frontier for the RTC adoption staircase.

writing_exemplar.why: Its RTC analysis connects ill-conditioning, latent-factor tails, heterogeneous timing, and implausible unadjusted matrix-completion estimates in one applied motivation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: State-policy panels are small and ill-conditioned -> a few factors explain most but not all untreated variation -> nominal low-rank intervals omit aligned tail bias -> report an event-curve sensitivity band and its RTC breakdown frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Use nuclear-norm initialization followed by least-squares singular-space refinement and its approximate-factor linearization without sample splitting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest inferential treatment of approximate low rank for causal panel completion and supplies the stochastic expansion to augment with worst-case tail bias.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over diversified projections and the explicit correction for bias caused by an over-estimated low-rank space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its central phenomenon, small extra directions causing first-order bias rather than only variance, is structurally the same obstacle as an unmodeled singular-value tail.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a studentized sup-t band from a joint covariance law and combine it with an explicit misspecification-bias radius.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution must report one whole event path with a common stochastic critical value after adding a horizon-coupled bias allowance.

open_problems.open_problem: For the eligible event-time ATT under staggered MNAR low-rank outcomes, when does averaging treated units within adoption cohorts before Choi--Yuan completion strictly improve asymptotic variance over completing unit or block targets first and then aggregating, without changing the estimand?

source_refs.claim: The discussion argues that combine-before-apply can have larger effective sample size than split-apply-combine and specifically suggests that it may improve Choi--Yuan ATT estimation.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael and Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association, discussion paper

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that staggered synthetic-control error depends on both unit-specific and pooled imbalance and that optimizing only one component can create bias.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael, Avi Feller, and Jesse Rothstein
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that inference for matrix linear forms depends on alignment with singular spaces, indicating why averaging before nonlinear completion need not equal averaging completed cells.
source_refs.author: Dong Xia and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Nuclear-norm regularization and singular-space estimation are nonlinear, so cohort averaging before completion changes estimated factor geometry and is not algebraically equivalent to averaging Proposition A.4 block outputs afterward. Ben-Michael--Feller state the efficiency conjecture, but the event-time target also changes its eligible cohorts with horizon and reuses donors across cohorts. The first proof step is to derive comparable influence arrays for both procedures under one primitive MNAR low-rank class, then establish an exact covariance ordering that includes shared donor cells rather than an independence approximation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient condition in cohort sizes, factor and loading geometry, and heteroskedastic cell variances under which the combine-before-apply estimator has weakly smaller event-curve covariance, together with an attaining estimator and joint limit law.

writing_exemplar.why: Its split-apply-combine versus combine-apply narrative states the efficiency tension without implying that the characterization is already known.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Choi--Yuan split staircase missingness into estimable blocks -> ATT aggregation supplies replication across treated units -> averaging before nonlinear imputation may improve effective sample size -> characterize when that gain survives event-time eligibility and shared donors

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose error into unit-specific and pooled balance components and derive the partially pooled estimator by optimizing both.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives a structurally analogous comparison between individual-first and pooled-first counterfactual construction under staggered adoption.

method_exemplars.technique: Use low-rank projection and singular-space perturbation to derive the variance of a general matrix linear form from its alignment with latent spaces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cohort event-time ATT is a structured linear form whose variance comparison must account for how pre-aggregation changes singular-space alignment.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive both candidate estimators from the same block-MNAR debiasing calculation and retain their exact observed-cell coefficients.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A valid efficiency ordering requires the common primitive model and exact influence accounting supplied by Choi--Yuan.

open_problems.open_problem: Can regularization, rank, and Choi--Yuan block-size choices be selected by an adoption-pattern-respecting procedure while preserving uniform influence representations and simultaneous event-curve coverage?

source_refs.claim: The discussion identifies hyperparameter selection as unresolved: random observed-cell holdouts do not reproduce structured missingness, while pre-period holdouts designed for block adoption may not extend to other patterns.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael and Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association, discussion paper

source_refs.claim: The paper proposes nuclear-norm matrix completion for causal panels and cross-validation based on held-out observed cells, supplying the prominent tuning baseline whose validation loss may mismatch a staggered adoption staircase.
source_refs.author: Susan Athey, Mohsen Bayati, Nikolay Doudchenko, Guido Imbens, and Khashayar Khosravi
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Diversified projections yield scalar linear-functional inference without consistently estimating rank, but do not establish post-selection growing-event-curve coverage for Choi--Yuan staircase blocks.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: The destination is not prediction-optimal tuning: simultaneous inference requires the selected fit to obey one uniform linearization and covariance-consistency statement on every eligible cohort-horizon block. Ben-Michael--Feller explain why ordinary cellwise cross-validation targets the wrong missingness geometry, while data-dependent tuning changes the remainder and can reuse residuals entering the multiplier covariance. The first changed proof step is a uniform oracle or stability inequality for a staircase-preserving validation loss jointly over the tuning grid and event horizons.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adoption-mimicking cross-fit or validation selector for penalty, rank upper bound, and block size, together with an oracle inequality and a post-selection uniform influence-and-multiplier theorem guaranteeing simultaneous event-curve coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames tuning as a deployment barrier created by structured rather than random missingness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Choi--Yuan inference depends on regularization and splitting choices -> random-cell validation does not emulate staggered missing counterfactual blocks -> practitioners tune from the same panel used for inference -> design a staircase-aware selector with valid whole-curve uncertainty

method_exemplars.technique: Use diversified projections and an over-specified-rank bias correction to avoid requiring consistency of discrete rank selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses inferential instability from unknown low rank and exposes the ridge-type bias caused by over-estimating the factor space.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the adaptive multiplier-band proof that controls data-chosen resolution levels through uniform coupling and anti-concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Choi--Yuan penalty and block grid plays the same inferential role as a data-selected resolution level, but its stability must be proved under staircase missingness.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace random observed-cell holdout by pseudo-adoption block holdout and prove that its loss controls the event-target prediction norm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest existing causal-panel tuning construction and therefore the natural baseline to modify.

literature_map:
Choi and Yuan (2024, JASA, arXiv:2308.02364) establish debiased scalar/block inference for low-rank matrix completion under structured MNAR and weak signals.
Ben-Michael and Feller (2026, JASA discussion, arXiv:2602.21314) identify event-time aggregation, staggered heteroskedastic variance, tuning, and diagnostics as Choi--Yuan's statistical last-mile gaps.
Their event-time section isolates the core tension: eligible exposure-duration effects aggregate different calendar columns and therefore different right factors.
Their RTC-law analysis supplies a live application with 44 states, adoption spread over 29 years, heterogeneous pre-period lengths, strong heteroskedasticity, and severe ill-conditioning.
Athey et al. (2021, JASA, arXiv:1710.10251) introduce causal-panel nuclear-norm completion and a random-cell validation baseline, but not growing event-curve coverage.
Bai and Ng (2021, JASA, arXiv:1910.06677) and Xiong and Pelger (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1910.08273) provide factor-based imputation and scalar inferential theory under missing panels.
Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2307.16370) give no-sample-splitting low-rank completion inference for entries and an average treatment effect under approximate factors.
Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026, JASA, arXiv:2311.16440) avoid consistent rank estimation via diversified projections and reveal non-negligible ridge-type bias from rank over-specification.
Xia and Yuan (2021, JRSSB, arXiv:1909.00116) derive debiased inference for general matrix linear forms and show variance depends on singular-space alignment.
Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, JRSSB, arXiv:1912.03290) define staggered synthetic-control event estimands and expose separate-versus-pooled balance, with only approximate bootstrap inference.
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics) prove multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous bands for staggered DiD event paths, a close inferential template but not a low-rank MNAR result.
Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:2108.12419) give robust and efficient event-study estimation under parallel-trends structure, not factor-completion structure.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1212.6906) provide Gaussian and multiplier approximation for correlated high-dimensional maxima once a vector influence sum is available.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1303.7152) show how Gaussian anti-concentration converts uniform linearization into honest adaptive bands.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1912.10529) and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Koike (2023, Annals of Applied Probability, arXiv:2012.09513) sharpen high-dimensional approximation rates, but no located paper constructs sharp counterarrays inside the Choi--Yuan low-rank staggered-MNAR class.
